title: Bruno
product: Bruno: open-source, Git-native, offline API client for REST, GraphQL, gRPC and WebSocket, with paid support tiers for teams.
target_customer: Engineering and QA teams of 2-50 who keep API requests in a shared Postman or Insomnia workspace and either lost free collaboration or cannot sync to a vendor cloud.
adjacent_icp: API providers who publish a ready-to-run collection for their developers alongside their docs.
search_scope: Public English and Portuguese web pages: vendor docs, GitHub discussions and repos, a vendor community forum, and a company engineering blog. No social profiles.
methodology: Read Bruno's home and pricing pages, then ran 8 web searches across switching, pain, workaround and timing buckets from the devtools query pack and fetched 10 pages. Every evidence quote was copied from the fetched page text and re-checked by finalize.py.
search_queries_used: Insomnia 8 requires login account github issue local collections lost
Postman Scratch Pad deprecated offline lightweight API client alternative
Postman free plan change 2026 single user collaboration team pricing

verdict: Yes, with clear timing. Postman's March 2026 one-user Free plan and its deprecated Scratch Pad create a dated trigger for small teams, and one IT services firm has already published a switch to Bruno. Segment and partner signals are strong; this no-people run lists no individuals by design.

segments.name: Small teams on Postman's Free plan after the March 2026 one-user limit
segments.pain_signal: Postman's March 2026 plan change limits the Free plan to one user, so a team sharing a free workspace now has to buy seats or move.
segments.evidence: With the new plans, the Free plan is limited to one user and can’t create a team.
segments.why_fit: Bruno collections are plain files in the team's Git repo, so sharing them needs no per-seat workspace; the core app is free and open source.
segments.why_now: The change took effect in March 2026; legacy-plan teams move at renewal, so the decision point is still arriving for many of them.
segments.content_angle: Searchable: a 'Postman free plan one user limit: what small teams can do' guide that walks through exporting a shared workspace and committing it as a Bruno collection.
target_keywords: share postman collection without paid plan
suggested_channels: Reply-when-relevant in r/webdev and r/QualityAssurance threads about the change
proof_points: Postman's own docs: the Free plan is limited to one user and can't create a team
Bruno's pricing FAQ: no account or login, collaboration through any Git provider
segments.caution: Postman's statement is about its plan structure, not about churn; how many teams actually leave is unmeasured.

segments.name: Insomnia users blocked by forced cloud login
segments.pain_signal: Teams report being unable to test against their own local servers because Insomnia required a login to reach saved requests.
segments.evidence: Currently our team is sitting here unable to use Insomnia to test our APIs that hit against our own local servers. Why? Because we need to login, for no reason.
segments.why_fit: Bruno has no account or login and keeps collections on disk, which removes the failure described: saved work behind a login server.
segments.why_now: The discussion lists eight linked issues about forced login for local-only content; the pattern recurs across Insomnia 8.x releases rather than being one outage.
segments.source_title: Remove Forced Login to Access APIs to Unrelated Server · Kong/insomnia · Discussion #7362
segments.content_angle: Shareable: an 'Insomnia to Bruno in ten minutes' page that leads with 'your requests never sit behind a login server', plus an importer walkthrough.
proof_points: Kong/insomnia discussion #7362 links eight issues on forced login for local-only content
Bruno pricing FAQ: there's no concept of an account or a login
segments.caution: Signal dated May 2024; Kong may have changed login behaviour since. Do not comment on Kong's tracker to promote Bruno.

segments.name: Developers whose company blocks API-client cloud sync
segments.pain_signal: Developers at organisations with security policies against cloud sync ask for the full Postman feature set offline.
segments.evidence: We do not want to use the scratch pad. We want to be able to benefit from the full feature set of Postman while working offline. We cannot use it online for security reasons.
segments.why_fit: Bruno is offline-first with no cloud component, so the security objection to syncing collections does not arise.
segments.why_now: The thread has stayed active for years (last activity 2025-07-08 per the page metadata), and Postman has since deprecated the Scratch Pad that was its offline answer.
segments.source_title: Using Postman with Z-Scaler - Page 5 - Help Hub - Postman Community
segments.content_angle: Searchable: a security-review one-pager ('what leaves the machine: nothing') that a developer can forward to their security team.
suggested_channels: Bruno docs: security and data handling
proof_points: Postman community thread: 'We cannot use it online for security reasons'
Bruno pricing FAQ: no cloud component for syncing or storage
segments.caution: The quoted post is from 2022; the thread's later activity shows the topic persists but not the poster's current situation.

segments.name: Former Postman Scratch Pad users who worked without an account
segments.pain_signal: Postman's offline, account-free workspace is deprecated and receives no updates, bug fixes or security updates.
segments.evidence: The Scratch Pad is deprecated and no longer supported. The Scratch Pad is being discontinued and won’t receive any updates, bug fixes, or security updates.
segments.why_fit: Bruno covers what the Scratch Pad did (local collections, environments, scripts) without an account, and adds Git-based sharing.
segments.why_now: Scratch Pad is gone from Postman v10.18 and later; remaining users are on unpatched versions or the reduced lightweight client.
segments.source_title: Build and send requests offline using the Scratch Pad | Postman Docs
segments.content_angle: Searchable: 'Postman Scratch Pad replacement' landing page comparing what the Scratch Pad, Postman's lightweight client and Bruno each keep locally.
proof_points: Postman docs: Scratch Pad is no longer available in Postman v10.18 and later
Bruno pricing FAQ: no account or login
segments.caution: Overlaps with the cloud-sync segment; the difference is motive (convenience vs policy). Keep one content piece per motive.

companies.name: NashTech
companies.pain_signal: A NashTech project team could not renew its Postman license and the client had strict data-residency rules, so it moved the project to Bruno.
companies.evidence: We couldn’t renew the Postman license for this project. There was no budget for enterprise SSO seats. Browser-extension-only usage wasn’t an option either. Our client had strict data-residency rules.
companies.why_fit: A delivery firm already running Bruno on a client project can standardise it across other client engagements with the same data-residency constraints; Bruno gains a reference deployment in services work.
companies.why_now: The write-up was published on 2026-07-29 after two weeks on a real project, so the evaluation is fresh.
companies.source_title: Saying goodbye to Postman: Why we switched to Bruno - NashTech Blog
companies.contact_path: NashTech's public 'Get in touch' page linked from its blog
companies.bd_angle: Your QA team moved a client project from Postman to Bruno because of licence cost and data-residency rules. Other client projects likely share those constraints. Would a short call on rolling Bruno out as a standard option across engagements, with support terms, be useful?
companies.what_to_propose: A 30-minute call with the QA practice to scope a multi-project rollout and a case study.
companies.caution: One project team's experience, not a company-wide decision; the blog post is a practitioner write-up.

companies.name: Consultar.IO
companies.pain_signal: An API provider already publishes its public API collection in Bruno's OpenCollection format with a one-click open button.
companies.evidence: Essa é a coleção do Bruno (OpenCollection) para as APIs do Consultar.IO. Clique no botão ou faça o clone do repositório e abra o repositório no Bruno.
companies.why_fit: Each API provider shipping a Bruno collection puts Bruno in front of that provider's developers; a showcase listing gives the provider extra discovery.
companies.why_now: The collection repo is live and linked from the provider's docs (docs.consultar.io/opencollection).
companies.source_title: GitHub - consultar-io/opencollection: Coleção OpenCollection para as APIs do Consultar.IO
companies.contact_path: Issues on the public consultar-io/opencollection repository
companies.bd_angle: You already publish your APIs as a Bruno OpenCollection with a one-click open button. We'd like to feature it as a reference collection for Portuguese-language APIs and link back to your docs.
companies.what_to_propose: Permission to list the collection in a public showcase of provider-maintained Bruno collections.
companies.caution: Small repository (1 star when fetched); value is as a pattern to replicate with more providers, not as one large account.

patterns.title: Saved work behind a vendor login
patterns.insight: Insomnia's forced login, Postman's sync requirement and the Scratch Pad deprecation are the same complaint. Lead with 'collections are files you own'.

patterns.title: Security or data-residency rules block cloud sync
patterns.insight: The NashTech client and the Postman forum thread both cite policy, not preference. A forwardable security page is worth more than a feature list.

patterns.title: Paying per seat to share requests
patterns.insight: Postman's one-user Free plan and NashTech's unrenewable licence both turn collaboration into a seat cost; Git-based sharing answers it directly.

competitive_context.switching_barriers: Existing collections, environments and pm.* scripts; Bruno's script API (bru/req/res) differs, so test scripts need porting.
competitive_context.differentiation_angle: No account, no cloud: collections live in the team's Git repository and are reviewed in pull requests like code.

outreach_plan.angle: Own the 'I lost free team sharing / I can't sync to the cloud' moment with migration content, then turn one services firm and a few API providers into public references.
outreach_plan.first_step: Publish the Postman Free one-user-limit migration guide and contact NashTech through its public contact page.
outreach_plan.follow_up: Ship the forwardable security one-pager; open an issue on the Consultar.IO collection repo asking to feature it.
outreach_plan.success: One partner call booked, one provider collection featured, and the migration guide indexed within seven days.
channels_to_prioritize: Warm BD via public contact page
outreach_plan.personalization_notes: Quote each source's own constraint back (licence renewal, data residency, forced login). Never name the people who posted in the threads.

limits: No-people run: Individuals were not researched; forum and GitHub posters are not named anywhere.
